preamble: To mark the publication of puzzle No 22,000, I dedicate this to the Guardian's setters in acknowledgement of all the pleasure they have given me as a solver.

clue.text: Angry about Chifonie's 17? Then get on, seeing state of play

indicators.note: about means going around, so the cross word wraps around the setter's initial

parts.note: sore can mean angry or aggrieved

indicators.note: 17-down is ORIGINAL, and the original of a setter's name is its opening letter

parts.note: Chifonie was a Guardian setter
to board a bus or ship is to get on it

explanation.surface: An irritated solver mulls over one of Chifonie's puzzles before getting on with the game.
explanation.walkthrough: In this tribute puzzle each setter's name stands in place, and '17' (ORIGINAL) asks for their initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoreboard displays the current score, which is the state of play in a match.

clue.text: Publish second-rate load of corn? It may obviate stuffiness!

parts.note: to air views is to make them public
B grade, the second class
a rick is a stack of corn or hay

explanation.surface: Talk of putting out a poor-quality heap of grain, then a cheerful remark about fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: An airbrick is a perforated brick set in a wall to let air through, preventing a room from becoming stuffy or damp.

clue.text: Have great respect for Paul, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to hold someone in deep esteem
second meaning: Paul ..., the American patriot of the midnight ride

explanation.walkthrough: Paul is also a Guardian setter, so the clue reads as admiration for him; 'perhaps' marks Paul as one example of a person surnamed thus.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere is to venerate; Paul Revere was the silversmith who warned of British troops in 1775.

clue.text: Cunning 1 and 17 of Logodaedalus — why disheartened about those?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the trimmed question word goes round the others
17-down is ORIGINAL, so the original of a setter's name is its first letter

parts.note: the middle letter of this question word is removed
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: losing its heart, a short word keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: Logodaedalus was a Guardian setter

explanation.surface: A puzzled solver asks why Logodaedalus's clues are so tricky.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' looks like a reference to 1-down, but it is just the numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wily is crafty and full of tricks, the same as cunning.

clue.text: Rocking cradle during delay, lacking a way to be assertive

indicators.note: during places one thing in the midst of another
lacking says the letter a is dropped from the word before

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a rocking cradle moves to and fro, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A parent rocks the cradle while waiting through some delay.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the A from DELAY to get DELY, then put the rearranged CRADLE in its middle: DE-CLARED-LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Declaredly is an adverb meaning openly or avowedly, a manner of speaking assertively.

clue.text: Orlando's latest? Fine — whack in few varied with hint of colour

indicators.note: the latest letter of a name is its final one

parts.note: Orlando was a Guardian setter

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is put inside another
varied means changed about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the three letters rearranged
to whack is to hit
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A query about Orlando's newest work, answered with a remark about a few changes and a touch of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-white describes white tinged slightly with grey or yellow, so it has just a hint of colour.

clue.text: Source of despondency, nowhere near completing Shed

definitions.text: Source of despondency, nowhere near completing
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ... of Despond, the bog Christian falls into early in The Pilgrim's Progress, long before he completes his journey
second meaning: to cast off, as a snake does its skin

explanation.surface: Despair at being far from finishing a puzzle by Shed, a Guardian setter.
explanation.walkthrough: Shed is also a Guardian setter, which disguises the verb. In Bunyan's allegory the Slough of Despond lies near the start of the pilgrim's road.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a swamp, hence Bunyan's despairing bog; as a verb it means cast off dead skin.

clue.text: The 17 puzzle by Gordius?

parts.note: surface reading: the original crossword set by Gordius, a Guardian setter
setter's reading: King Gordius of Phrygia tied the intricate tangle Alexander the Great cut through

explanation.surface: A solver asks after the very first puzzle Gordius set.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is ORIGINAL: the Gordian knot was the original puzzle tied by Gordius, solved only by cutting it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gordian knot, tied by Gordius, is the proverbial intractable problem, so it is his original puzzle.

clue.text: Araucaria's other name — Cinephile, distributed elsewhere

indicators.note: letters spread out to other positions are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Araucaria, the Guardian's most celebrated setter, is reimagined as a film buff who has moved away.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria looks like the setter, but here it is the tree genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Araucaria araucana, the monkey puzzle tree, is also called the Chile pine after its native country.

clue.text: Fidelio's 17 — one concocted left inside as a criminal

indicators.note: something concocted is made up anew, so the letters are mixed
17-down is ORIGINAL, so the setter's name supplies its opening letter

parts.note: Fidelio was a Guardian setter

indicators.note: inside places one letter within the mixed word

parts.note: the three letters rearranged
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A setter's original work is condemned as a fabrication by someone left on the inside of a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon is a person convicted of a serious crime, so a criminal.

clue.text: Something Rover perpetrated — all at sea?

definitions.text: Something Rover perpetrated — all at sea?

parts.note: surface reading: a piece of work by Rover, a Guardian setter, perhaps leaving solvers confused
setter's reading: a sea rover is a pirate, and piracy is theft carried out on the water

explanation.surface: Solvers are left bewildered by whatever Rover has put together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all at sea' suggests confusion, but it really places the crime on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover is an old word for pirate, and piracy is theft committed on the high seas.

clue.text: Rules out going Dutch in this case

parts.note: laws are rules
uit is the Dutch word for out

explanation.surface: Splitting the bill is ruled out on this occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going Dutch' looks like sharing costs; here it means translate the word before into Dutch.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawsuit is a legal case brought before a court.

clue.text: Patience needed to find alternative for one of Bunthorne's

definitions.text: Patience needed to find alternative for one of Bunthorne's

parts.words: Patience needed to find alternative for one of Bunthorne's
parts.note: surface reading: you need patience to find a substitute for one of Bunthorne's clues, Bunthorne being a Guardian setter
setter's reading: Gilbert and Sullivan's operetta Patience has an alternative title, '... or Bunthorne's ...'

explanation.surface: It takes patience to work out an answer to one of Bunthorne's clues.
explanation.walkthrough: The operetta's full title is Patience, or Bunthorne's Bride; the setter Bunthorne took his name from its poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in the subtitle of Patience is the woman Bunthorne hopes to wed.

clue.text: Person summoned — one to enter solution of eg Hendra's missing Down

indicators.note: the numeral joins the other letters before they are worked out together
a solution dissolves things and mixes them, so these letters are rearranged
missing tells us the following letter is dropped

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
Hendra was a Guardian setter; taken as written
D is the grid abbreviation for down

explanation.surface: Someone is called in to solve one of Hendra's puzzles that lacks a down clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove D from EG HENDRAS, add I, and rearrange. A garnishee is a legal term for a person summoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A garnishee is a debtor served with a legal notice to hold funds for a creditor, so a person summoned.

clue.text: Type of verse having most of scope in French

indicators.note: in says the shortened word sits within the other

parts.note: Gallic means French

indicators.note: most of a word is all of it but its final letter

parts.note: ambit means scope or extent

explanation.surface: A kind of poem said to have most of its range in French.
explanation.walkthrough: The shortened word for scope splits the French adjective after its I, so the container lands mid-word rather than at a natural break.
explanation.definitionFit: Galliambic is a classical metre, used by Catullus in his poem Attis, named after the Galli priests of Cybele.

clue.text: Having to guess when Enigmatist gets out of order!

definitions.note: the participle stands in for the activity of guessing

indicators.note: out of order means not in sequence, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Enigmatist is a Guardian setter; taken as written

explanation.surface: Solvers are left guessing whenever Enigmatist is misbehaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Estimating means judging roughly without full information, which is guessing.

clue.text: This expression of appreciation has been given the nod

definitions.text: This expression of appreciation has been given the nod

parts.note: surface reading: the preamble's thanks to the Guardian's setters
setter's reading: a nod is a token of recognition, given in thanks

explanation.surface: The setter's thanks in the preamble has been approved for publication.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer appears in the preamble itself: the puzzle is dedicated 'in acknowledgement' of the setters.
explanation.definitionFit: An acknowledgement is an expression of thanks or recognition, often given with a nod of the head.

clue.text: First description of Manchester appearing as Guardian's leader

definitions.meaning: first meaning: earliest, the very first

definitions.text: description of Manchester appearing as Guardian's leader
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the paper began as the Manchester Guardian, so Manchester was its earlier name's lead word

explanation.surface: Manchester once headed the Guardian's title.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper was the Manchester Guardian until 1959; throughout this puzzle 17 also means a setter's initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Original means earliest or first, and Manchester was part of the newspaper's founding title.

clue.text: Sounded as if they are in agreement and went in order to look

indicators.note: sounded as if means the word that follows is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: those voting yes are the ayes
left is the past tense of leave, so went away

explanation.surface: People who seemed to agree then marched off in an orderly way to have a look.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes left is a military command telling marching troops to turn their heads to the left, so an order to look.

clue.text: The two-facedness of Janus?

parts.note: surface reading: Janus, a Guardian setter, is accused of being deceitful
setter's reading: the Roman god Janus has two faces, so his nature is literally doubled

explanation.surface: A question about whether Janus, setter or god, is untrustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: The word's root duplex means twofold, so it suits the two-faced god literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Duplicity means deceitfulness, being two-faced, and comes from the Latin for double.

clue.text: One from Gemini?

parts.note: surface reading: someone born under the star sign of the twins
setter's reading: one of the twin brothers the constellation is named after, also a star in it

explanation.walkthrough: Gemini looks like a horoscope sign; the answer is one of the mythical twins, the other being Castor, and also a Guardian setter's pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Castor and Pollux are the twins of Gemini, and Pollux is the constellation's brightest star.

clue.text: Taupi's 17 and two thirds of Mercury generate some heat

indicators.note: keeping two thirds of a six-letter name drops its last third
17-down is ORIGINAL, so the setter's name contributes its first letter

parts.note: Taupi was a Guardian setter
Hermes is the Greek counterpart of the Roman god Mercury

explanation.surface: Two planetary or godly sources combine to produce warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition's 'generate some heat' is loose: the answer is a quantity of heat rather than an act of generating it.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat, used in Britain for billing gas, so it is a measure of heat.

clue.text: Some ideas associated with Quantum?

parts.note: surface reading: notions linked with Quantum, a Guardian setter
setter's reading: the physics of quanta, a body of ideas explaining the atom

explanation.walkthrough: Quantum looks like the setter; the question mark points to the famous phrase from physics.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a set of ideas explaining something, and quantum theory is the best-known example.

clue.text: Does Rufus sometimes substitute his second definition?

definitions.text: Does Rufus sometimes substitute his second definition?

parts.words: Does Rufus sometimes substitute his second definition?
parts.note: surface reading: does Rufus, a Guardian setter known for double definitions, sometimes swap in another meaning?
setter's reading: Rufus, the red one, was the nickname of the Conqueror's son who became King of England in 1087; his given name is another way to define him

explanation.surface: A solver wonders whether Rufus ever swaps his second meaning for something else.
explanation.walkthrough: Rufus was famous for double definitions; here his name is King William II's epithet, so the king's name is a second definition of Rufus.
explanation.definitionFit: William Rufus, the red-faced son of the Conqueror, is identified by both names, so each can define the other.

clue.text: A little bit hazy with middle bit of Crispa and Plodge's 17

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with

indicators.note: the middle bit of a six-letter name is its central pair

parts.note: Crispa was a Guardian setter

indicators.note: 17-down is ORIGINAL, so the setter's name gives its first letter

parts.note: Plodge was a Guardian setter

explanation.surface: Memories of two setters' puzzles are somewhat vague.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisp is a thin trail of smoke or mist, a small hazy fragment.

clue.text: Juggled with letters, cluing this fish

indicators.note: things juggled are tossed about and land in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter describes how the clue for a fish was made by shuffling its letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes its own working: rearranging 'letters' gives the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The sterlet is a small sturgeon of the Caspian and Black Sea basins, prized for caviar.

clue.text: Tailpiece — recollect Custos, so sadly missed

indicators.note: to re-collect is to gather up again in a fresh arrangement
something missed is left out of the name

parts.note: Custos was a Guardian setter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A closing remembrance of the setter Custos, whose loss is mourned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollect' and 'sadly missed' read as a tribute. Take SO out of CUSTOS and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short tail of a hare, rabbit or deer, literally a piece at the tail.

clue.text: Recalled shorter answer, stuck with leading pair from Audreus, in the bath!

indicators.note: stuck with suggests something lodged within the other piece
recalled means called back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ans is the short form of answer

indicators.note: the leading pair are the first two letters of the name

parts.note: Audreus was a Guardian setter

explanation.surface: Someone thinks of a short answer to an Audreus clue while soaking in the tub.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauna is a steam bath, a Finnish hot-air room for bathing.

clue.text: One vital point put over about Don Pasquale's last "pain-killer"?

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: about means around, so the turned word surrounds the rest
put over means turned the other way, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: the nub is the crux, the vital point
a don is a university teacher, a prof

indicators.note: the last of a name is its final letter

parts.note: Don Pasquale was a Guardian setter

explanation.surface: Don Pasquale, Donizetti's comic opera, ends with someone needing relief from pain.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Pasquale, the setter, is split: 'Don' gives PROF and the final letter of Pasquale is E.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibuprofen is a common anti-inflammatory drug taken to relieve pain.
